title: Pause tap
rule: Input runs before movement. A UI button consumes the touch and sets Paused. Movement only runs while Playing.
steps: Playing: a touch lands on Pause.
UI consumes the touch and changes state.
choices: The character moves once, then pauses
No movement and no attack
No movement, but the same tap attacks
explanations: Movement checks Paused after input.
The consumed touch cannot also reach gameplay.
The UI consumed that touch.

title: Two phones
rule: A moving wall advances a fixed distance on each update. Both phones run for one second, one at 30 FPS and one at 60 FPS.
steps: Both start at the same position.
The update adds a fixed distance, not distance × elapsed time.
choices: The 60 FPS wall moves twice as far
Both walls move equally far
The 30 FPS wall moves twice as far
explanations: Twice as many updates produce twice the movement.
Equal movement would need elapsed-time scaling.
The 30 FPS phone runs fewer updates.

title: Coin ownership
rule: A coin sets its own collected flag before awarding points. Coin A reports three contacts, then coin B reports one.
steps: A is uncollected: accept and mark A.
choices: Only A pays
A pays three times; B once
A and B each pay once
explanations: Each coin owns its own flag.
A is already marked after its first callback.
Duplicate A contacts do not suppress B.

title: Protection window
rule: A hit immediately starts one second of protection. Contacts arrive at 0, 0.2 and 1.1 seconds.
choices: First and third contacts hurt
Only the first contact hurts
All contacts hurt
explanations: The middle contact is protected; the last is not.
Protection lasts one second, not forever.
Contacts inside the window do not hurt.

title: Exit order
rule: The update checks the exit before collecting a key. The character touches both in the same update. The exit requires the key.
choices: Finish immediately
Collect the key, but need another exit check
Neither event happens
explanations: At exit check time the key was absent.
The next exit check can now succeed.
The exit check does not cancel key collection.

title: Paused timer
rule: A timer uses game time. A menu animation uses real time. The game pauses for two seconds.
steps: Game time pauses; real time continues.
choices: Both keep advancing
Both stop
Timer stops; menu animation continues
explanations: The timer uses game time.
The menu animation uses real time.
Each system obeys its selected clock.

title: Finish twice
rule: The first exit callback enters Result and awards a card. Every later callback first checks that state is Playing.
steps: Exit callback 2 arrives before the next render.
choices: Two cards are awarded
One card is awarded
Neither card is awarded until rendering
explanations: The second callback sees Result.
The state transition protects the reward.
Rendering shows data; it does not grant rewards.

title: Old display
rule: Input changes score. Update keeps it. Render accidentally reads a saved copy from before input.
choices: State and display both show one
State stays zero; display shows one
State is one; display still shows zero
explanations: Render is reading the old copy.
Input changed the actual state.
The display is stale, even though the rule succeeded.

title: One gesture
rule: After movement passes the gesture threshold, the larger axis wins and locks this gesture. Horizontal distance wins first; the finger then bends upward.
choices: Only the horizontal action happens
Horizontal action and jump both happen
The jump replaces the horizontal action
explanations: The same gesture was already committed.
A locked gesture does not dispatch a second action.
Changing direction does not undo a committed input.

title: Healing order
rule: The player is below maximum health. A pickup heals, clamps health to maximum, marks itself consumed, then a hazard deals damage.
choices: Health stays at maximum
Health ends below maximum; pickup stays consumed
The pickup heals again after the hit
explanations: The later hit still applies.
Consumption and health are separate state changes.
A consumed pickup cannot heal again.

title: Checkpoint
rule: A level checkpoints position and collected keys. A failure restores both. A key collected after the checkpoint is not saved.
steps: Save a checkpoint without a key.
choices: Return with the new key
Return at the start with the key
Return at the checkpoint without the new key
explanations: The new key was never checkpointed.
The checkpoint saves position too.
Both fields restore from the saved checkpoint.

title: Held touch
rule: Move is held while a finger touches the control. Release and app-background events both clear the held state.
steps: The app enters the background before release.
choices: Movement remains released
Movement stays held until another tap
The app must restart the level
explanations: The background event cleared held input.
There is no held input left to resume.
Clearing input does not reset level progress.
